title: Constant local dimension of a locally finite type field groupoid
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $U=\operatorname{Spec}K$ be an $S$-scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: functorially on test schemes, $s,t$ give source and target, $e$ identities, $i$ inverses and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ composition [def-pc-fibre-product], satisfying the groupoid axioms. Suppose $s$ and $t$ are locally of finite type, meaning that their composites with every etale scheme chart of $R$ are locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For an algebraic space $X$, $|X|$ denotes the set of morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ with $L$ a field, two of them identified when their pullbacks to some common field extension agree. Define $\dim_x(X)=\dim_v(V)$ for $x\in|X|$ using an etale scheme chart $V\to X$ and a point $v$ above $x$, where $\dim_v(V)$ is the infimum of Krull dimensions of open neighbourhoods of $v$, and define $\dim X=\sup_{x\in|X|}\dim_x(X)$. Then $\dim_r(R)=\dim R$ for every $r\in|R|$. In particular, for a group algebraic space $H$ over $K$ that is locally of finite type (the case $s=t$ equal to the structural map), $\dim_h(H)=\dim H$ for every $h\in|H|$.

source.place: Tag 06FD (lemma-groupoid-on-field-locally-finite-type-dimension), clause (1), and Tag 06FE (lemma-group-over-field-locally-finite-type-dimension), clause (1); dimension conventions Tags 04N5 and 04N6.

proof.text: First record the one-field-base-change calculation needed below. Let $a:\operatorname{Spec}L\to U$ be any field-valued point and put $F_a=R\times_{s,U,a}\operatorname{Spec}L$. The fibre-product and atlas clauses of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] give this algebraic space and a surjective etale chart $V_L=V\times_U\operatorname{Spec}L\to F_a$ from any surjective etale scheme chart $V\to R$. For a point $z\in|F_a|$ above $x\in|R|$, choose $w\in V_L$ above $z$ and let $v\in V$ be its image. The scheme map $V\to U$ is locally of finite type by the hypothesis on $s$. Apply [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] to $V\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. Since these bases have one point with residue fields $K,L$, its fibres are $V,V_L$ themselves, and it gives $\dim_w(V_L)=\dim_v(V)$. The chart definitions in the statement therefore give $\dim_z(F_a)=\dim_x(R)$. This is a direct specialization of the cited scheme equality, not a comparison of local-ring dimensions. Only one field base change of a locally finite type scheme map is used.

source.place: Tag 02FY (morphisms-lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change), part (1), specialized to field spectra; chart calculation underlying spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04NS, part (1).

proof.text: Fix $r,r_0\in|R|$ and choose field-valued representatives $a_0:\operatorname{Spec}L_0\to R$ and $b_0:\operatorname{Spec}L_1\to R$. Their images under $t$ are equal as point classes of $U=\operatorname{Spec}K$, whose only prime is $(0)$. By the definition of equality of point classes in the statement, there are field extensions into a common field $L$ for which the induced maps $a,b:\operatorname{Spec}L\to R$ satisfy $t a=t b$ as morphisms. They still represent $r,r_0$. Put $u=s a$ and $v=s b$. Both are maps $\operatorname{Spec}L\to U$, but need not be equal: the two resulting embeddings $K\to L$ must be kept distinct.

source.place: Tag 0452 (lemma-two-fibres), common-field reduction; more-groupoids.tex Tags 02YF (lemma-two-fibres), parts (1)-(2), and 04LP (lemma-groupoid-on-field-homogeneous).

proof.text: Form $F_u=R\times_{s,U,u}\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $F_v=R\times_{s,U,v}\operatorname{Spec}L$ using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The maps $a,b$ lift to $L$-valued points $\widetilde a,\widetilde b$ of these spaces. Use the convention that $c(f,g)=f\circ g$. Then $q=c(i a,b)$ is an arrow from $v$ to $u$. On every $L$-scheme $T$, the rule $f\mapsto c(f,q_T)$ defines a map $F_u(T)\to F_v(T)$, since $s(f)=u_T=t(q_T)$. Its inverse is $g\mapsto c(g,i(q_T))$: associativity and the inverse and identity axioms give $(f\circ q)\circ q^{-1}=f$ and $(g\circ q^{-1})\circ q=g$. The formulas commute with pullback of test schemes, so define inverse morphisms of algebraic spaces over $L$. Also $a\circ(a^{-1}\circ b)=b$, so this isomorphism carries $\widetilde a$ to $\widetilde b$. Compose any etale scheme chart of $F_u$ with this isomorphism to obtain a chart of $F_v$ with the same scheme and chart point. The definition of dimension thus gives $\dim_{\widetilde a}(F_u)=\dim_{\widetilde b}(F_v)$. Applying Step 1 to the two embeddings $u,v$ yields $\dim_r(R)=\dim_{r_0}(R)$.

source.place: Tag 0452 (lemma-two-fibres), source-fibre identification; explicit pointed right-translation version of more-groupoids.tex Tag 02YF (1)-(2) and Tag 04LP. Groupoid identities are written out here.

proof.text: The identity $e:U\to R$ supplies a point $r_0$, so $|R|$ is nonempty. Step 3 says that all terms of the defining supremum $\dim R=\sup_{r\in|R|}\dim_r(R)$ equal $\dim_{r_0}(R)$. Their supremum is this same value, proving the first assertion. For a group algebraic space $H$ over $K$, take $U=\operatorname{Spec}K$, $R=H$, $s=t$ its structural map, and $c,e,i$ its multiplication, identity and inverse. The group identities are exactly the groupoid identities in this case, and local finite type gives both required hypotheses. Apply the first assertion to get $\dim_h(H)=\dim H$.
